Mar del Plata lies on the Atlantic Ocean, south of Buenos Aires. Its long coastline, beaches and opportunities for strolling around town make it a suitable stop after several days in Argentina's agricultural regions.

We suggest using the city as a base for a trip to Balcarce and keeping the evening free for an independent walk by the ocean. This itinerary combines professional meetings with relaxed leisure time, without changing hotels every day. For delegations, we arrange accommodation, transfers and schedules so that trips out of town fit naturally alongside life in a major seaside resort.

Maras is known for the salt ponds set into a slope in the Sacred Valley area. The small pools form a dense pattern of terraces, their pale surfaces contrasting with the surrounding mountain slopes and agricultural landscapes.

The salt-producing areas are closely linked to local work and traditional livelihoods. A visit adds a different perspective on the use of natural resources to an exploration of Moray and the valley's other landmarks. Maras shows how mountain terrain can become a working landscape and how traditional production forms a distinctive part of the Andean scenery.

Trips to the caves depart from Puerto Río Tranquilo. The journey brings visitors close to the stone arches and their natural patterns. Whether the boat can enter individual grottoes, and how long the trip lasts, depend on the weather, water conditions and the crew's decisions.

Mariana is a historic town in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais, often visited together with Ouro Preto. Its streets, squares, old houses and churches retain the atmosphere of settlements that grew during the gold-mining era. A walk through the centre offers a quieter, more intimate view of colonial Brazil.

The gold-mining story continues beyond the centre: some itineraries include a visit to the Passagem Mine. This is a separate excursion stop to allow time for when planning a visit. Mariana fits especially well into a journey through the historic towns of Minas Gerais, where architecture, crafts and the region's mining past come together.

Maringá serves as the commercial centre of the Visconde de Mauá area. A visit to the village can be combined with walks through the surroundings, where forest trails, rivers and natural pools are found.

The village features in itineraries alongside Vila da Maromba. Here, the mountain portion of the journey is enriched by a glimpse of everyday life in small local communities.
